entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Costa Rican Civil War was a pivotal event in modern Costa Rican history. 

The conflict began on March 12, 1948, when the People's Party, led by José Figueres Ferrer, clashed with the National Liberation Party, led by Otilio Ulate Blanco, over issues of land reform and government representation. 

The war lasted for 44 days, ending on April 24, 1948, with the signing of the Treaty of Peace and Union. This treaty established a new constitution, which would go on to shape the country's future. 

One of the lasting legacies of the Costa Rican Civil War was the establishment of a new constitution, which would serve as a model for future democratic reforms in the region. As José Figueres Ferrer noted, 'Our victory is not a triumph of one party over another, but a triumph of the people over the politicians.'
